title: How the Antikythera Mechanism Worked
summary: A geared bronze device from the 2nd century BC that modelled the movements of the sun, moon and planets. Nothing of comparable complexity appears again for a thousand years.

title: The Great Molasses Flood
summary: In 1919 a storage tank burst in Boston and sent a wave of molasses through the North End at 35 mph, killing 21 people.

title: Why We Sleep in Cycles
summary: Humans move through roughly 90 minute cycles of non-REM and REM sleep, and waking mid-cycle explains the grogginess of a short night.

title: The Invention of the Shipping Container
summary: One standard steel box cut the cost of loading a ship by 97% and quietly rewired where the world makes things.

title: How Roman Concrete Survives the Sea
summary: Volcanic ash and seawater react to grow new mineral crystals inside Roman harbour concrete, so the structures get stronger with age.

title: The Quiet Rise of the Night Train
summary: Sleeper services are returning across Europe as passengers trade speed for a night of sleep and a city centre arrival.

title: A Brief History of the Bicycle
summary: From a wooden horse you pushed with your feet to the safety bicycle that gave women independence and paved the way for the car.

title: The Map That Changed Epidemiology
summary: John Snow plotted cholera deaths around a Soho water pump in 1854 and invented modern disease mapping in the process.

title: Why Cathedral Builders Used Flying Buttresses
summary: Pushing the roof load outward let walls become windows, which is the entire reason Gothic cathedrals glow.

title: The Deep Sea Is Still Mostly Unmapped
summary: Roughly a quarter of the ocean floor has been surveyed at modern resolution. The rest is inferred from satellites.

title: How Sourdough Starter Actually Works
summary: Wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria form a stable community that outcompetes spoilage organisms and leavens bread without commercial yeast.

title: The Economics of a Cup of Coffee
summary: The farmer who grows the bean earns a few cents of a four dollar cup, and most of the value is captured after the beans leave the country.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey of Failure Modes
summary: RAG systems fail mostly at retrieval, not generation: chunking choices, embedding mismatch and reranking errors dominate measured error.

title: Small Models, Long Contexts: A Practical Trade-off Study
summary: A 7B model with a well-tuned retriever outperforms a 70B model on document QA at a fraction of the serving cost.

title: Measuring Urban Heat Islands with Cheap Sensors
summary: A network of 200 low-cost nodes shows intra-city temperature swings of 7C between tree-lined streets and asphalt yards.

title: Why Battery Chemistries Plateau
summary: Energy density improvements stall when the cathode becomes the limiting electrode, shifting research toward sodium and iron chemistries.

title: Sleep Debt Does Not Repay Itself
summary: Recovery sleep restores subjective alertness but not metabolic markers, suggesting cumulative cost from chronic short sleep.

title: Ask HN: What did you learn too late in your career?
summary: Hundreds of practitioners on compounding skills, saying no, and the cost of optimising for the wrong ladder.

title: Ask HN: How do you actually read a long book a week?
summary: A thread of concrete habits: fixed slots, paper over screens, and abandoning books after 50 pages without guilt.

title: Ask HN: Best way to learn a city on foot?
summary: Locals describe route-planning by river and market, and why the second visit to a neighbourhood is where it opens up.

title: Ask HN: Anyone else switched from podcasts to reading?
summary: Commuters compare retention, note-taking and the pleasure of finishing something at exactly the moment you arrive.

title: Ask HN: What's a small tool that changed your mornings?
summary: A short thread on timers, single-purpose devices and the surprising value of laying clothes out the night before.

title: Ask HN: How do you keep up with research outside your field?
summary: Practitioners describe following two people rather than twenty feeds, and reading abstracts until one sentence surprises them.

title: Ask HN: What broke your commute habit?
summary: Short answers on route changes, phone notifications and the moment a commute stops being a protected block of time.

title: The Attention Economy Is a Design Problem
summary: When the product is attention, interfaces optimise for interruption rather than completion, which is why reading anything long feels like a fight.

title: Meditations, Book Two
summary: Marcus Aurelius on the discipline of the present moment, the shortness of life, and doing the next right thing without applause.

title: The Problems of Philosophy, Chapter One
summary: Bertrand Russell asks whether there is any knowledge in the world so certain that no reasonable person could doubt it.

title: The Republic, Book Seven
summary: The allegory of the cave: prisoners mistake shadows for reality, and the one who leaves is blinded twice.

title: The Prophet, On Work
summary: Kahlil Gibran on labour as love made visible, and on the difference between working with affection and working with aversion.

title: The Yellow Wallpaper
summary: Charlotte Perkins Gilman's short story of a woman confined for rest, whose wallpaper slowly becomes the only thing she can read.

title: How Cities Cool Themselves
summary: Trees, reflective roofs and permeable pavement measurably reduce street-level heat, but only where shade reaches the pavement people walk on.

title: A Short History of Time Zones
summary: Railways forced the world to abandon local solar time, and the boundaries drawn in 1884 still cause arguments today.

title: Why Bread Costs What It Costs
summary: Wheat prices are set by futures markets far from the bakery, and a harvest failure three continents away shows up in your loaf within weeks.

title: The Physics of Walking
summary: A walking human is an inverted pendulum that recovers most of its energy from each fall, which is why walking is cheaper than it looks.

title: The Origins of the Public Library
summary: Free lending libraries were a radical nineteenth-century idea: that reading should not depend on being able to afford books.

title: How Noise Shapes a Neighbourhood
summary: Chronic traffic noise raises stress hormones and lowers reading comprehension in children, and it is measured in decibels most cities never map.

title: The Case Against the Open-Plan Office
summary: Studies consistently find more interruptions and less face-to-face conversation in open offices than in cubicles.

title: Container Gardens That Survive Winter
summary: Roots freeze before leaves do, so the trick is insulating the pot rather than the plant.

title: Ask HN: Reading projects that actually stuck
summary: People describe finishing projects only when the reading was tied to a commute, a class, or a person they wanted to argue with.

title: Ask HN: How do you pick what to listen to on a short drive?
summary: Short answers favour single-topic episodes over news roundups, because a roundup always ends mid-story.

title: Language Learning in Twenty-Minute Blocks
summary: Spaced practice in short daily blocks outperforms one long weekly session for vocabulary retention at three months.

title: The Surprisingly Old Idea of Working From Home
summary: Before the office was invented, most work was domestic. The commute is the historical anomaly.

title: Cicero on Old Age, Part One
summary: Cicero argues that old age is only burdensome to those who have not learned to use their own company.
